title: inference-microbreak-log-marcus
content:
Morning microbreak log — quick brain dump (non-blocking)
Date: 2026-03-12 morning sprint
Context: odd bump in 95th pct latency on small-baseline tenant during a canary window (2:14–2:27 UTC). Not the usual KV cache churn pattern.

Quick summary:
- Observed: 95th increased from ~120ms -> ~420ms for text-generation route (gpt-like-8b-quant) at ~120 qps sustained.
- Error rate: 0.2% 503 spikes correlated with the latency spikes (not sustained).
- Affected path: hosted routed -> region fallback -> dedicated fallback (policy: cost-priority).
- Suspected: interplay between small-batch autoscaling and model variant fallback + stale KV entries leading to cache thrash.

Repro notes (what I ran locally to try to reproduce):
1) curl load generator (short seq lengths ~32, p50 ~80ms locally):
   for i in {1..400}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" -d '{"model":"gpt-like-8b-quant","input":"foo"}'; done
2) with --concurrency 40, saw p95 ~350ms on staging for 10s window (matches symptom).
3) sampling with X-Redwood-Route header to force primary/dedicated variant toggles latency pattern.

Logs & quick grep (snips):
- runtime logs: "prefix_cache_miss: true, kv_evictions: 12, active_batches: 3" (2:15:22)
- scheduler: "scale_down_candidate: pool-A, last_used: 2026-03-12T02:14:57Z"
- fallback: "route_decision=fallback, reason=capacity_pressure, target_variant=dense25q"

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Autoscaler oscillation + small-batch fallback: rapid route switch triggers reloading of quantized weights and flushes prefetch caches -> transient 200–500ms stalls.
B) KV cache thrash for long-lived conversations: prefix cache performed poorly when requests spread across variants (cache key mismatch across quantized variants).
C) Scheduling priority inversion: low-priority threads holding GPU memory while higher-priority request waits for kernel init.

Immediate short-term mitigations to test (quick experiments):
- Pin route to primary variant for the canary tenant for next 30m and watch p95. (TODO: add route override in console, user: canary-ops).
- Temporarily increase min-pool-size for pool-A from 1 -> 2 to reduce cold inits during brief load bumps.
- Add a small sleep (50ms) on fallback decision to avoid thrash loop (simulate throttling).

Longer-term TODOs (for next sprint):
- [ ] Add metric: "variant_switch_rate" per tenant (histogram) to detect thrash automatically.
- [ ] Normalize KV-cache keys across compatible quantized variants or add cross-variant cache layer.
- [ ] Improve autoscaler hysteresis logic for tiny pools (pool size <=3).
- [ ] Add a trace tag in requests when kernel init is triggered (so we can correlate traces with init overhead).
- [ ] PR to runtime: ensure async kernel loads don't block request dispatch thread (see PR 982 for related changes).

Notes to self:
- Talk to Leah (collab) after lunch — she has a different reproducer that toggles sequence length (may rule out pure cold-start).
- Check SRE alert config: current p95 alarm config ignores short bursts <2m — we probably want a burst rule for canary tenants.

Quick commands / queries to run later:
- k get pods -n runtime | grep pool-A && kubectl logs -f pod/<suspect> --since=10m | grep kernel_init
- Query metrics explorer: sum(rate(prefix_cache_evictions[5m])) by (pool, tenant)
- Trace lookup: trace_id from request sample -> link to jaeger: https://jaeger.redwood.test/trace/{{TRACE_ID}}

Unresolved questions (brain dump):
- Does fallback cause full process-level weight reload or just kernel rebind? (ask runtime core team).
- Are quantized variants considered cache-compatible at prefix-key layer? I think not today.
- Any bias in tenant routing rules that would cause same tenant to oscillate between pools? need to audit policy config.

Random smaller items (notes to archive later):
- micro-bench: 8b-quant kernel init ~120–180ms from cold on A100-80GB; 4b ~60–90ms.
- check if we have a cheap prewarmer that can prefetch kernels during low load windows.

Next steps (today):
1) Push pin override for canary tenant (Marcus). 10m observation window.
2) Run increased min-pool-size test (coord w/ infra, Leah).
3) Add metric query dashboard snippet for variant_switch_rate (quick grafana panel).
4) Capture 3 sample traces (with trace ids) and attach to INF-4312.

End of morning microbreak — this is mostly a scratchpad; will convert to a short postmortem if the pattern repeats.

-- Marcus
